en.title: 7 TV Villains Dominating the 2020s So Far
en.summary: From manipulative masterminds to terrifying forces of nature, these are the 2020s' most compelling antagonists who have redefined what it means to be a great TV villain.
en.body:
The 2020s have gifted us with a pantheon of truly unforgettable villains, characters so compelling they often steal the show. These aren't just one-dimensional bad guys; they're complex figures whose motivations and actions have left an indelible mark on television.

## 1. Homelander (The Boys)
Antony Starr's portrayal of this seemingly perfect superhero is a masterclass in corrupted power. Homelander isn't just evil; he's a terrifyingly petulant god-child whose immense abilities are matched only by his profound insecurity and sociopathic tendencies, making him the benchmark for 2020s villainy.

## 2. Wilson Fisk (Daredevil: Born Again Season 2)
While details for "Daredevil: Born Again Season 2" are still emerging, the web research points to Wilson Fisk, aka Kingpin, continuing his reign of terror. His calculated brutality and imposing presence, even in the face of renewed challenges, solidify his status as a formidable antagonist who operates with chilling precision.

## 3. Sofia Falcone (Gotham's Lingering Shadow)
Cristin Milioti brings a captivating depth to Sofia Falcone, a villain who feels remarkably human despite her sinister actions. Her presence in "Gotham's Lingering Shadow" and subsequent Penguin-verse continuations highlights her as a complex, wounded individual whose ambition knows no bounds, making her a standout character.

## 4. Nolan Grayson (Invincible)
J.K. Simmons delivered a performance that was both shocking and deeply impactful as Nolan Grayson, aka Omni-Man. His journey from beloved father figure to galactic conqueror in "Invincible" showcases a villain whose betrayal cuts to the core, redefining the stakes of superhero narratives.

## 5. The Manipulative Patriarch (Specific show TBD)
Several shows in the 2020s have featured chillingly effective patriarchs who wield familial influence as a weapon. These characters, often driven by ego and a twisted sense of control, create compelling dramatic tension by blurring the lines between love and manipulation, making their downfall all the more satisfying.

## 6. The Supernatural Threat (Specific show TBD)
From ancient evils to otherworldly entities, the 2020s have seen a surge in compelling supernatural villains. These antagonists tap into primal fears, offering terrifying challenges that test the limits of our heroes and audiences alike, often with visually stunning and conceptually intricate designs.

## 7. The Cult Leader (Specific show TBD)
Characters who build devoted followings through charisma and insidious ideology have become a recurring nightmare this decade. These leaders exploit vulnerability and sow discord, presenting a unique threat that is as psychological as it is physical, forcing heroes to confront not just an individual, but a movement.

Bottom Line: These villains aren't just obstacles; they're complex characters who elevate their respective series, proving that the best antagonists are often the most compelling.

content_raw: Television's most memorable villains of the 2020s range from manipulative family patriarchs to supernatural threats, all with unforgettable performances.
